html:
Baguirmi was a kingdom south-east of Lake Chad, in what is now southern Chad, founded around 1522 with its capital at Massenya. The map shows it from 1530 to 1800.

Its kings became Muslims in the later 1500s. Baguirmi lived by farming along the Chari River and by raiding the peoples to the south for captives, who were kept as slaves or sold north. It was squeezed between stronger neighbours and often paid tribute to Bornu or Wadai, which sacked Massenya in 1871.

In 1893 the warlord Rabih az-Zubayr destroyed the capital. The sultan placed Baguirmi under French protection in 1897, and it became part of French Equatorial Africa.
